svg.title: Depth of Skin/Soft Tissue Infections
svg.text: Depth of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections — Superficial to Deep
Each band spans the full width to show the anatomic depth of each diagnosis
Epidermis — Impetigo (honey-colored crust, S aureus/S pyogenes)
Upper Dermis + Superficial Lymphatics — Erysipelas (sharp demarcation, S pyogenes)
Deep Dermis + Subcutaneous Tissue — Cellulitis (spreading, S pyogenes/S aureus)
Deep layers, walled-off — Abscess (pus collection, S aureus)
Fascia — Necrotizing Fasciitis (pain out of proportion, surgical emergency)
Anaerobes / S pyogenes / S aureus (MRSA) — "flesh-eating bacteria"
Rule of thumb: deeper infection → more severe → more urgent surgical intervention
"Pain out of proportion to exam" is the classic red flag for necrotizing fasciitis
(nerves are destroyed before the skin looks abnormal — exterior appearance can be deceiving)
